defects.where: ref and front views, trunk front strand
defects.fix: The carved knotwork band is missing entirely. Add a raised flat band about 0.5 m wide on the front strand, spiralling roughly 3/4 turn from z=2.6 m to the cut top at z=6.5 m, with a 5 cm border groove each side and 6-7 square/diamond knot motifs about 0.4 m across, incised 4-6 cm deep with a darker recess colour.

defects.where: all views, trunk (z=3.5-6.5 m)
defects.fix: Trunk reads as one lumpy twisted tube, not a braid. Build 3-4 separate strands, each 0.9-1.1 m in diameter, wrapping about one full turn over the trunk height, with V-grooves 15-25 cm deep between them so each strand is traceable from the top down into a root.

defects.where: ref, front and back views, trunk top
defects.fix: Top is an open hollow cup with a dark hole and a thin wavy rim. Replace with solid flat saw-cut strand ends, staggered +/-0.2 m in height and slightly tilted, no cavity.

defects.where: all views, root skirt
defects.fix: Roots are far too thin and too many: about 25+ tendrils 0.3-0.45 m thick against about 12 primaries in the reference. Cut to about 12 primary roots, 0.8-1.0 m thick where they leave the trunk, about 0.5 m at mid-run and 0.25-0.3 m just before the tip split; each should be the continuation of a trunk strand.

defects.where: ref and front views, skirt mass between z=1 m and z=3.5 m
defects.fix: Skirt is an airy cage with see-through gaps; the reference is a dense cone of roots packed shoulder to shoulder with a darker second layer behind. Close the gaps in the upper two thirds by thickening the primaries and adding 6-8 inner-layer roots under them, so no ground or background shows through above z=1 m.

defects.where: all views, trunk waist around z=4-4.5 m
defects.fix: Trunk necks in to about 1.5 m wide at the waist; the reference widens steadily downward (about 1.9 m at the top, about 2.7 m at z=4 m) and merges into the root shoulders without a pinch. Widen the lower trunk and start the flare at about z=3.5 m.

defects.where: ref, right and left views, root paths
defects.fix: Roots run as near-straight radial spokes with small jittery kinks. Give each primary broad S-curves (wavelength 2-3 m, sideways amplitude 0.4-0.6 m) and make each cross over or under a neighbour 1-2 times so the skirt reads as braided.

defects.where: all views, root tips at the ground
defects.fix: Tips are mostly single thin curling tendrils. Split each primary in its last 1.5-2 m into 2-4 rootlets 0.15-0.25 m thick, fanned 20-35 degrees apart, lying flat on z=0 like claws and ending in sharp points.

defects.where: all views, bark surface of trunk and roots
defects.fix: No bark relief, only large smooth triangles 0.5-1 m across on the trunk. Add lengthwise bark plates: grooves 3-5 cm deep along each strand and root every 0.25-0.4 m around the circumference, cross-breaks every 0.5-1 m along the length, and chiselled facets 0.2-0.3 m in size.

defects.where: all views, bark colour
defects.fix: Bark is pale bone-beige, far lighter than the reference. Darken to a warm olive-taupe (about #7A6F58), with crevices about #4A4435 and facet highlights about #A39A80; add per-facet value variation of about +/-10% and darkening in the grooves.

defects.where: all views, moss patches
defects.fix: Moss is hard-edged saturated green camouflage blotches scattered evenly, including on vertical faces and root sides. Make it a soft desaturated olive tint (about #6B7038) blended with a noisy soft edge, limited to up-facing surfaces and crevices of the upper roots and trunk, about 15% coverage.

defects.where: right and left views, footprint
defects.fix: Footprint is 9.76 x 8.27 m inside a 10.5 x 10.5 m envelope; once the roots are thickened, let the longest 3-4 roots reach 5.0-5.2 m from the centre in y as well, so the skirt is not visibly narrower from the side.

note: scene-recon route, first round. Geometry: Trellis 2 from refs/trunk_roots.png (191k tris -> 40k, yaw 235, 53 detached islands dropped). Knob-fixable here: bark colour, moss, bark relief shading. Not knob-fixable (they are the Trellis mesh itself): missing knot band, single-tube trunk, hollow top, thin and too many roots, airy skirt, waist, root paths, tips. Stopped after one round for the user's review.

defects.where: ref and front views, rune vs recessed panel (also left view)
defects.fix: The cyan knot is not inside the recess: it sits about 0.15-0.2 m toward image-left, lying over the left frame leg and bare stone, and leaves a ~0.15 m strip of unlit grey knot relief showing on the right of the panel. In the left view the panel shows only grey relief, with cyan slivers at the frame edge and on the opposite silhouette. Put the emissive strokes on the panel floor with the same centre line and facing as the panel, fully inside the inner frame with a 5-8 cm margin. Keep one knot only: either make the carved relief itself emissive or delete the grey relief.

defects.where: all views, stone material
defects.fix: Stone is untextured flat pale warm off-white (value about 75-80%). The reference is mid-grey granite (value about 50-55%, near sRGB 135,135,128) with painted mottling, darker crevices between facets, lighter highlights along facet ridges, fine dark crack lines and a cooler blue-grey tint toward the base. Darken the base colour, add low-contrast mottle at 10-30 cm scale plus fine speckle, darken concave areas and lighten convex edges (pointiness/AO), roughness about 0.85.

defects.where: right, left and back views, overall depth
defects.fix: The stone is as deep as it is wide (1.33 m deep against 0.6 m intended; 1.30 m wide against 1.1 m) and reads as a round tooth or cone instead of a slab-like standing stone. Scale depth to about 0.6-0.65 m (x0.47) and width to about 1.1 m (x0.85), keep 3.2 m height. Check the bounding box is not inflated by the misplaced rune or the frame slab.

defects.where: back view upper-right edge; right view lower-right base; back view lower-left base
defects.fix: A paper-thin flat fin about 0.5 m tall sticks out past the stone outline at the upper right of the back view, and open dark vertical slits about 0.6-0.8 m tall show at the base in the right and back views, where the front/frame slab does not meet the body. Union the frame slab into the body, weld the seam, and delete loose zero-thickness faces so the back and sides are one closed rock.

defects.where: ref view, panel floor
defects.fix: The recess floor is the same pale grey as the body and covered in zigzag relief. In the reference it is flat, smoother and darker blue-grey (about sRGB 95,115,125), which makes the rune stand out and picks up cyan bounce. Make a flat floor recessed 5-6 cm with a darker blue-grey material and a faint cyan falloff next to the strokes.

defects.where: ref view, panel frame
defects.fix: The frame is a single soft, wobbly ridge. The reference has a crisp double-stepped border: an outer raised band about 10-12 cm wide with a chamfer, then an inner bevel about 4 cm down to the floor, with a sharp pointed-arch top whose peak is about 16% down from the stone tip (here about 22%) and straight legs running almost to the ground, closing to a point at the bottom with two short vertical grooves either side. Build the frame from clean planar strips rather than the decimated rock mesh, keep its edges straight, and raise the arch peak about 0.2 m.

defects.where: ref view, rune strokes and pattern
defects.fix: Strokes are thin (about 3 cm), flat, saturated cyan lines with three small diamond centres and a dense weave. The reference bands are about 6-7 cm wide, pale frosty white-cyan (about sRGB 190,235,240) with soft mottled texture and a slightly deeper cyan rim, forming two stacked lozenge loops with two diamond centres and pointed finials top and bottom, filling the panel to within about 5 cm of the frame. Double the stroke width, lighten and desaturate the emission, add noise variation in strength, cut the strokes as inlaid channels with 1 cm bevels, and simplify to two lozenges.

defects.where: all views, rock faceting (surface detail and style)
defects.fix: The surface is uniformly small random flat-shaded triangles (5-15 cm), giving a crumpled-paper low-poly look. The reference is hand-painted chunky stylised stone with large chiselled planes 20-50 cm across, crisp bevelled ridges, a few smaller chips and thin cracks. Use fewer, larger planar facets (cut the body with 12-20 planes or planar-decimate to about 150-250 faces), bevel ridges 1-2 cm, add 5-8 crack lines and 3-4 chips 5-10 cm deep on silhouette edges, and shade smooth with sharp edges instead of per-triangle flat shading.

defects.where: ref view, top of stone
defects.fix: The tip is a rounded blob. The reference has a distinct asymmetric point at about the left third of the width, a near-vertical left side and a large flat facet sloping about 35 degrees down to the right shoulder. Sharpen the apex, move it about 0.15 m left of centre, and form the shoulder from 2-3 big planes.

defects.where: ref view, lower half outline
defects.fix: The right side has a bump at mid-height and the left side tapers in too early toward the base. The reference is widest at about 65% of the way down, then narrows slightly to a chipped, lightly undercut foot. Move the widest girth down and add 2-3 chips at the foot.

note: scene-recon route, first round. Geometry: Trellis 2 from refs/runestone.png (99k tris -> 5k, yaw 130). Trellis made a wedge with TWO rune panels (the second, on the far side, is what the judge sees unlit in the left view) and its own knot relief, which the front-projected GPT mask does not follow. Knob-fixable here: stone value and mottle (the pre-judge colour pass overshot to pale), rune position / stroke width / colour, panel floor tint, planar facets and shading, depth and width by per-axis scale, loose thin faces. Not knob-fixable: second panel, soft frame, tip and outline (the Trellis mesh). Stopped after one round for the user's review.

defects.where: ref and front views, front trunk strand, z=4.2-6.4 m
defects.fix: The carved knotwork band is still missing entirely. Add a raised flat band about 0.5 m wide spiralling roughly a third of a turn up the front strand over about 2.2 m, with 5-6 square/diamond knot motifs about 0.4 m each, incised 5-8 cm deep, a 6-8 cm border ridge on each side and darker grooves.

defects.where: all views, trunk z=3.8-6.5 m
defects.fix: Trunk still reads as one twisted tube with a shallow spiral crease. Build it from 3-4 separate strands, each 0.6-0.8 m thick, wound half a turn to one turn over the trunk height, with V-grooves 0.15-0.25 m deep between them. Let each strand run on downward as a primary root so the braid flows into the skirt with no shoulder.

defects.where: all views, whole surface
defects.fix: Surface is a smooth subdivided clay sculpt with round sausage cross-sections; the reference is faceted low-poly with flat chiselled planes 0.2-0.5 m across and hard edges. Remove subdivision and smooth shading, use 6-8 sided cross-sections with jittered ring vertices and flat shading, and add 2-3 planar chisel cuts per metre of root.

defects.where: all views, root ends at the ground
defects.fix: Tips are blunt rounded stubs 0.3-0.4 m thick, one or two per root, several curling upward. Split each primary into 2-4 rootlets 1-1.5 m long, fanned 20-40 degrees apart and lying flat, each tapering to a sharp point under 0.05 m.

defects.where: ref, right and left views, skirt core under the trunk, z=0.5-3 m
defects.fix: A dark hollow still shows between roots that arch out like spider legs. Add 5-6 inner roots dropping steeply within 1.5 m of the axis to fill the cavity, and keep neighbouring primaries touching or overlapping down to about z=2 m.

defects.where: all views, primary roots along their length
defects.fix: Primaries are about 0.5-0.6 m thick at the trunk, stay almost the same thickness to the tip, and number about 14-16. Use about 12 primaries, 0.8-0.9 m at the trunk, tapering steadily to about 0.3 m where they split.

defects.where: ref and front views, root paths in the skirt
defects.fix: Roots still run mostly radially and join by Y-forks; almost none pass over another. Give each primary a broad S-curve of 0.5-0.8 m amplitude and route at least 4-5 clear over/under crossings on the front face, continuing the trunk braid downward.

defects.where: all views, trunk top z=5.3-6.5 m
defects.fix: Top is still an open cup with a dark hole, a flared wavy lip about 1.45 m wide over a neck about 1.1 m wide, and moss on the rim. The hole will be hidden by the crown, but the flared lip and neck will not. Make the trunk about 1.3 m wide at the top, widening without a pinch to about 1.9 m at z=4 m, close it with a flat cap at z=6.5 m, and remove the rim moss.

defects.where: all views, bark texture on trunk and roots
defects.fix: Bark is a fine pinstripe of lines 3-5 cm apart wrapping around the limbs like lathe marks. Replace it with lengthwise bark plates 0.2-0.4 m wide and 0.5-1 m long running along each strand and root, separated by crevices about 30% darker (about #4E4638).

defects.where: all views, moss on root shoulders and trunk base
defects.fix: Moss is now soft-edged and on up-facing surfaces, but is a saturated yellow-green (about #8C9A2E) in large patches. Shift it to a desaturated olive (about #6B6F45), blend it at 30-50% into the bark, and cut cover to 10-15%, concentrated in crevices of the upper roots.

defects.where: all views, bark base colour
defects.fix: Bark is now a warm tan (about #8E7B5C): close, but slightly too light and yellow and uniform. Move it to about #7A6F58 with a cooler grey-olive cast and vary value by 10-15% from plate to plate.

defects.where: right and left views, footprint
defects.fix: Footprint is 9.65 x 8.16 m, slightly smaller than last round and still 1.5 m narrower in depth. Lengthen the front and back roots by about 0.7 m each for a near-round footprint of about 9.6-10 m.

note: Knob round (free): inflate 10 cm + voxel skin, smooth shading, bark colour, bump, soft moss. +0.5. The judge's note flipped on shading (r01 'large smooth triangles' -> r02 'smooth clay sculpt, wants flat chiselled planes'). Remaining high defects are the Trellis mesh (band, braid, root tips, hollow core); knob-reachable next: planar facets instead of smooth, moss colour and cover, bark tone, bump scale.

defects.where: ref and front views, recessed panel floor
defects.fix: A translucent light-blue rectangular quad (about 0.45 m wide x 2.1 m tall) sits in front of the recess; its square corners spill over the frame's arch top and over the bottom point. Remove the rectangle/halo plane. Make the floor an opaque face cut to the same pointed-arch outline as the inner frame edge, sunk 4-6 cm, darker and less saturated (about sRGB 95,115,125). Any glow should come from the rune's emission only.

defects.where: ref and front views, panel and rune width
defects.fix: Recess is about 43% of the face width (about 0.47 m); the reference panel floor is about 55% (about 0.6 m) and the frame's outer edge about 65% (about 0.7 m). The rune is about 0.40 m wide against about 0.46 m in the reference, and covers about 52% of the stone height against about 59%. Widen the recess to about 0.6 m, scale the rune about 1.15x in X and 1.12x in Z, and leave a 5-7 cm margin to the frame.

defects.where: left view upper left edge and base; back view upper right edge
defects.fix: A thin light sliver/fin still stands at the upper right of the back view (about 2.3-2.8 m high), and the left view shows a dark crescent gap about 0.4 m long at 2.0-2.5 m height plus a dark vertical slit at the base (0-0.4 m). These read as an overlapping shell that does not meet the body. Boolean-union or bridge that shell into the body, bury its edge at least 3 cm, then remove interior faces and weld so no gap or knife-edge is visible from any view.

defects.where: all views, rock faceting
defects.fix: Facets are long vertical slivers (about 0.1-0.25 m wide x 0.8-1.5 m tall) with soft, barely readable ridges; the back and right side are nearly smooth, and the left view has a strip of small crumpled zigzag triangles on the side face. The reference has polygonal chiselled planes 20-50 cm across in both directions with crisp ridges. Cut the hull with 25-35 random planes 5-15 cm deep, keep facet aspect under 2:1, flat-shade, and add 6-8 chipped corners at the shoulders and base. Remove the crumpled strip.

defects.where: all views, stone material
defects.fix: Stone is light neutral grey (about sRGB 150-165 lit) with faint cloudy mottling only. The reference is darker, slightly warm olive-grey (about 135,135,128) with painted dark crack lines along facet borders, lighter ridge highlights, fine speckle, and a cool blue-green tint toward the base and around the panel. Darken the base colour about 15%, add ridge highlights (+15% value on a pointiness/bevel mask), cavity darkening (-25% on an AO mask), crack lines 1-2 cm wide on 0.3-0.5 m cells, and a blue-grey gradient over the bottom 0.6 m.

defects.where: ref and front views, panel frame
defects.fix: The frame is a soft low ridge; the double step only reads at the arch tip, the left leg fades into the body and the right leg reads as a broad flat slab about 0.2 m wide. The reference has two crisp nested bands (outer about 8 cm wide raised 4-5 cm, inner about 4 cm bevel) running the full height on both legs and converging to a point at the bottom, with a V notch in the stone below. Extrude a two-step pointed-arch profile with sharp unsmoothed edges and equal leg widths.

defects.where: ref and front views, rune material
defects.fix: The rune is a flat, uniform, near-white emissive (about sRGB 230,250,255) that reads as a decal. The reference bands are pale frosty cyan (about 190,230,235) with icy mottling, brighter cyan rims, and a soft glow onto the floor, cut 1-2 cm into the floor as channels. Lower emission about 40%, add noise of about +/-15% value, tint the band edges cyan (about 120,210,225), and inset the bands 1-2 cm.

defects.where: right and left views, side profile and crown
defects.fix: From the side the stone tapers to a needle tip (about 5 cm deep) and reads as a blade. The reference keeps a blunt faceted crown and visible side thickness up to the shoulders. Keep depth at 0.35 m or more up to 2.8 m height and make the crown about 0.25 m deep with 2-3 flat facets.

defects.where: ref view, base
defects.fix: The base ends in a flat cut with a curved, oval-looking footprint and a stepped ledge at the front right where the frame slab stops. The reference base is angular, with the bottom 0.3 m chamfered inward by about 0.1 m on the left and about 0.2 m on the right. Make the footprint an irregular 6-8 sided polygon, add 10-15 cm chamfers to the bottom edge, and blend the frame legs into the base.

defects.where: ref view, bottom of rune
defects.fix: The rune ends in three stacked chevrons. The reference ends with two long diagonal bands converging on a single pointed finial with a short central vertical stem. Replace the chevrons with that finial and stretch it to reach the panel's bottom point.

note: Knob round (free): per-axis scale to 1.1 x 0.65 x 3.2, voxel skin, 1800 tris + planar facets, stone colour, panel box from the median, mask v2, floor tint. +0.7, past the review gate.
